text:
The Kings are 7-12-2 and our numbers think they deserve a lot better. They have 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), but they have scored about seven fewer goals than those chances predict and allowed about seven and a half more. Our standings model has them seven points behind what their play has earned, as big a gap as you will find.

There are reasons for hope. Kevin Fiala is back, nine months after the frightening injury he suffered at the Olympics, and he has played since Nov. 13. The top line of Adrian Kempe, Artemi Panarin and Alex Laferriere has taken 62% of the expected goals and outscored teams 8-3. Erik Gustafsson returned with two points in Boston, and his pair with Brandt Clarke is the best on the blue line by chances.

Kempe also made news for the wrong reason, fined for a high stick on Toronto's Dakota Joshua before scoring the shootout winner in that game. Darcy Kuemper got the win.

At 4-6-0 in the last 10, patience is getting harder to sell, and Daily Faceoff is already asking whether the Kings could sell Drew Doughty. Our playoff odds have them at 28%. What we'd watch: whether Peter Laviolette's team starts converting a process that has been fine all along.
